cues.en: I've actually introduced you to the idea of scaling laws in math, physics and biology, and we had a code challenge on that topic.
cues.zh: 前面介紹過數學、物理、生物的尺度律，也做過程式挑戰。

cues.en: That was with counting the number of characters in tokens in different books and websites.
cues.zh: 就是計算不同書籍、網站中，詞元的字元數。

cues.en: That was called Zipf's law.
cues.zh: 叫齊夫定律。

cues.en: Now, in this video, I'm going to discuss the scaling laws that are seen in AI and how that relates to AI safety.
cues.zh: 這支談 AI 的尺度律，以及與安全的關係。

cues.en: And actually, I'm going to make the argument that there is a logical fallacy whereby people use past data to predict future outcomes.
cues.zh: 我也會主張，用過去資料預測未來，存在一種邏輯謬誤。

cues.en: And I'll show some analogies to explain why I think this reasoning is incorrect.
cues.zh: 用幾個類比，解釋為何認為推理不正確。

cues.en: I will also discuss why there might be so much hype around AI development and scaling.
cues.zh: 也會談，AI 發展與規模為何充滿炒作。

cues.en: Yeah, so these are two plots that I showed earlier in the course in the section about tokenization.
cues.zh: 這兩張，是前面斷詞章節的圖。

cues.en: The general idea of a scaling law is that there are certain phenomena in the physical and biological
cues.zh: 尺度律的一般概念，是物理、生物

cues.en: world that do not have a single characteristic scale at which they operate, but instead their frequency
cues.zh: 世界有些現象，沒有單一特徵尺度，

cues.en: or magnitude is proportional to their size or occurrence.
cues.zh: 頻率或量值，而與大小、出現情形成比例。

cues.en: Basically, any time you see a straight line in a log log plot that is taken as evidence of scaling laws.
cues.zh: 基本上，雙對數圖出現直線，就視為尺度律的證據。

cues.en: I also discussed that these are not laws, in the sense that they are required by some mathematical or physics equation.
cues.zh: 也說過，這不是數學或物理方程式必然要求的定律。

cues.en: Instead, scaling laws are actually just observations of phenomenon based on data that have already been collected in the past.
cues.zh: 而是根據過去已收集資料，觀察現象。

cues.en: They cannot necessarily be used to accurately predict the future in ways that other laws in physics can be used.
cues.zh: 不能必然像其他物理定律那樣，準確預測未來。

cues.en: The most famous scaling law in computer science is called Moore's Law.
cues.zh: 電腦科學最著名的，是摩爾定律。

cues.en: Moore's law says that the number of transistors on a microchip doubles approximately every two years or thereabouts.
cues.zh: 晶片電晶體數量，大約每兩年翻倍。

cues.en: Another interpretation is that the computing power per unit currency increases over time, and you could
cues.zh: 也可理解為，每單位金錢取得的算力，隨時間增加；

cues.en: also say that the cost of computing per flop halves every roughly every two years.
cues.zh: 或每次浮點運算的成本，大約每兩年減半。

cues.en: It's been a pretty consistent observation for the past century, or even a little bit more.
cues.zh: 過去一世紀，甚至更久，都相當一致。

cues.en: And it may continue into the future until we reach some physical or economic ceiling.
cues.zh: 未來也可能持續，直到物理或經濟上限。

cues.en: But here I also want to stress that Moore's Law is not the result of some natural physical process.
cues.zh: 但強調，這不是某種自然物理過程的結果。

cues.en: It's largely due to engineers trying to maintain Moore's Law.
cues.zh: 很大部分，是工程師努力維持。

cues.en: That is, people are working really hard on making transistors better or cheaper or smaller, specifically with the goal of maintaining Moore's Law.
cues.zh: 大家努力把電晶體做得更好、更便宜、更小，目標就是維持定律。

cues.en: So if economic forces would shift, then Moore's Law could stop happening at any moment.
cues.zh: 經濟力量改變，就可能隨時停止。

cues.en: Now let me tell you about scaling laws in Llms.
cues.zh: 現在談 LLM 尺度律。

cues.en: I have a question mark in parentheses up here, because AI is so new, and llms are so new that what
cues.zh: 標題括號裡有問號，因為 AI、LLM 很新，

cues.en: people refer to as scaling laws here are actually only based on a few years worth of data.
cues.zh: 所謂尺度律，實際只根據幾年資料。

cues.en: Contrast that with Moore's Law that I showed in the previous slide.
cues.zh: 對比上一張摩爾定律，

cues.en: That's based on over a century of data.
cues.zh: 基於超過一世紀資料。

cues.en: So a lot of excitement about scaling laws in law started from this paper several years ago.
cues.zh: 幾年前，這篇論文引起許多對 LLM 尺度律的熱情。

cues.en: Among other findings, they showed that plots that looked like this, where you have the test loss from
cues.zh: 其中顯示這種圖，y 軸是訓練 LLM 的

cues.en: training llms on the y axis and various parameters on the x axis.
cues.zh: 測試損失，x 軸是各種參數。

cues.en: So here in this plot, for example, you see the total number of parameters in the model.
cues.zh: 例如這張，是總參數量。

cues.en: Here you see the total data set size.
cues.zh: 這張是總資料集大小。

cues.en: And here on the left is the petaflops per day, which is basically the amount of GPU processing power that you can use during pre-training.
cues.zh: 左邊是每天 petaflops，基本上指預訓練可用的 GPU 算力。

cues.en: So all of these lines go straight down.
cues.zh: 線條都直直下降。

cues.en: And the interpretation was that, for example, as the data set size increases or the number of parameters increases, this line will go down.
cues.zh: 解讀是，資料集或參數量增加，線就下降，

cues.en: It will keep going down until the losses get to, I don't know, zero.
cues.zh: 持續下降，直到損失，譬如到零。

cues.en: Now, as I mentioned before, these data are based on past observations.
cues.zh: 但如前所說，這些都是過去觀察。

cues.en: They do not guarantee what's going to happen in the future.
cues.zh: 不保證未來。

cues.en: For example, it seems like humanity is running out of data to train these models on.
cues.zh: 例如，人類似乎快用完模型訓練資料。

cues.en: This is a graph from a company called epoch AI, and they've basically estimated here that we are fairly
cues.zh: 這是 Epoch AI 圖表，估計我們

cues.en: close to using up all of the useful training data that are available.
cues.zh: 很接近用完所有有用、可取得的訓練資料。

cues.en: Now, of course, the amount of text that is published online is massively increasing every day.
cues.zh: 當然，網路文字每天大量增加。

cues.en: But an increasing amount of online text is low quality.
cues.zh: 但低品質比例也增加。

cues.en: It's noisy, it's redundant, or it's just slop that is written by less capable.
cues.zh: 雜訊、重複，或能力較差模型寫的垃圾內容。

cues.en: So that's all low quality data that will only make the models worse.
cues.zh: 都是只會讓模型變差的低品質資料。

cues.en: So those kinds of data need to be filtered out.
cues.zh: 需要過濾。

cues.en: The point here is that these quantities like data set size and parameters, which also translates to compute power and storage.
cues.zh: 重點是，資料集大小、參數量，也代表算力與儲存，

cues.en: These are not abstract mathematical quantities that can increase to infinity.
cues.zh: 並不是能增加到無限大的抽象數學量。

cues.en: Instead, there are real world constraints on these parameters.
cues.zh: 現實有約束。

cues.en: And even aside from the practical constraints, infinite growth is just not reasonable to expect in a newly developing system.
cues.zh: 就算沒有實務限制，也不該期待新系統無限成長。

cues.en: For example, here is a chart of the average height in boys during development as a function of their age.
cues.zh: 例如，這是男孩平均身高隨年齡的發展圖。

cues.en: Now, when you look at these lines, if you really believe that scaling is constant, then you have to believe that these lines will continue to go up at the same rate.
cues.zh: 若真的相信成長尺度固定，就得相信這些線會以相同速度持續上升。

cues.en: And that would mean that you would have to believe that a 40 year old man should be somewhere around three meters tall.
cues.zh: 代表四十歲男性應該約三公尺高。

cues.en: That's almost ten feet tall.
cues.zh: 將近十英尺。

cues.en: Obviously that's not the case.
cues.zh: 顯然不是。

cues.en: So what's the problem here?
cues.zh: 問題在哪？

cues.en: What is wrong with my reasoning?
cues.zh: 推理哪裡錯？

cues.en: Well, I'm sure you know it has something to do with this blocked out bar over here.
cues.zh: 你應該知道，和這裡被遮住的長條有關。

cues.en: Now, the thing is that extrapolating from complex systems is very difficult and usually wrong.
cues.zh: 複雜系統外推很難，而且通常錯。

cues.en: There is a reason why you cannot predict the weather more than a week or two in advance.
cues.zh: 無法提前一、兩週以上預測天氣，是有原因的。

cues.en: Weather is a highly complex dynamical system, and so extrapolation out to a longer time window just doesn't work.
cues.zh: 天氣是高度複雜的動態系統，長時間外推不可行。

cues.en: Same thing for height and weight.
cues.zh: 身高、體重也一樣。

cues.en: And there are tons of other examples where extrapolating a nonlinear system will lead to incorrect and sometimes hilarious conclusions.
cues.zh: 還有很多例子，非線性系統外推，會產生錯誤、有時很好笑的結論。

cues.en: The difficulty here is that we live in the present moment, and predictions about future AI capabilities
cues.zh: 困難是，我們活在現在，未來能力的預測，

cues.en: are based on things that do not yet exist, like models with a thousand times as many parameters as what we have now.
cues.zh: 依據的是尚不存在的東西，例如參數比現在多一千倍的模型。

cues.en: So imagine that this is time on the x axis, and the y axis reflects some measure of AI capabilities.
cues.zh: 假設 x 軸時間，y 軸某種 AI 能力。

cues.en: Of course, at the very beginning of AI these capabilities were minimal, basically non extinct.
cues.zh: 最初能力很低，幾乎沒有。

cues.en: But then there was a rapid rise in capabilities in a short period of time.
cues.zh: 接著短時間快速上升。

cues.en: And presumably it levels off at some point, perhaps for practical or physical limitations, or maybe
cues.zh: 想必某時會趨平，也許因實務、物理限制，或

cues.en: just because intelligence itself, as we know it in neural or silicon systems, is just fundamentally limited by some upper ceiling.
cues.zh: 因神經或矽系統的智慧，本身有根本上限。

cues.en: So the question is, where are we right now with AI development?
cues.zh: 問題是，目前發展在哪個位置？

cues.en: If you think that we are here, then that means that there will be an explosive amount of growth and capabilities of AI systems.
cues.zh: 若在這裡，代表能力還會爆炸成長。

cues.en: But on the other hand, perhaps we are here, and all of the incredible explosive growth in AI capabilities
cues.zh: 但也許在這裡，驚人的成長

cues.en: is behind us, and the next versions will be just marginally better than what we have right now.
cues.zh: 已經過去，下一版只稍好一點。

cues.en: The problem is that we have no idea where we are on this graph, and we're not going to know until years into the future.
cues.zh: 問題是，不知道在哪，要等多年後才知道。

cues.en: And you can think about this graph for basically every kind of development of capabilities.
cues.zh: 基本上，任何能力發展都能想成這張圖。

cues.en: Just think about when you were first learning Python coding.
cues.zh: 想想初學 Python。

cues.en: There was a period of time where your coding skill just increased incredibly fast, and every week you are a much better coder than you were the week before.
cues.zh: 有段時間進步極快，每週都比上一週厲害很多。

cues.en: But at some point the gains become marginal.
cues.zh: 但某時變成邊際改善。

cues.en: And yeah, you're still improving your coding skills, but not really by that much.
cues.zh: 還是進步，只是沒那麼多。

cues.en: And you can say the same thing for learning a new language, learning how to play football, playing a new video game, and so on.
cues.zh: 學語言、踢球、玩新遊戲，也一樣。

cues.en: There's always a window of really steep learning curve, but that incredible rate of progress is just not sustainable.
cues.zh: 總有一段陡峭的學習期，但驚人速度無法持續。

cues.en: And at some point, you start getting diminishing returns where you put more and more work into learning and you're still learning.
cues.zh: 某時報酬遞減，花更多力氣，仍在學，

cues.en: You're still getting better, but not that much better.
cues.zh: 仍進步，卻沒那麼多。

cues.en: Now, to be super clear, I have no idea where on this graph A.I. development currently is.
cues.zh: 說清楚，我完全不知道現在 AI 在圖上哪裡。

cues.en: I do not know and no one else knows, but I do believe 100% that it is a fallacy.
cues.zh: 我不知道，也沒人知道，但百分之百相信，

cues.en: It is false reasoning simply to assume that we are down here just because that's what people who run AI companies tell us.
cues.zh: 只因 AI 公司負責人這麼說，就假定在這裡，是推理謬誤。

cues.en: Let me tell you another example that I think you will agree with.
cues.zh: 再舉一個你可能同意的例子。

cues.en: Think about what cell phones looked like in the year 2005 and what their capabilities were, and compared that to cell phones in 2015.
cues.zh: 想想 2005 手機的樣子、能力，再與 2015 比。

cues.en: So only ten years later, that span of ten years was absolutely transformative.
cues.zh: 只差十年，變化極大。

cues.en: Within those ten years, from 2005 to 2015, we got the iPhone and other smartphones.
cues.zh: 2005 到 2015，出現 iPhone 與其他智慧型手機。

cues.en: We got GPS in phones, we got high quality cameras, touch screens and uncountable number of apps and so on.
cues.zh: GPS、高品質相機、觸控螢幕、無數 App 等等。

cues.en: Okay, but now maybe you see where this is going.
cues.zh: 現在可能猜到我要說什麼。

cues.en: Think about the difference between a cell phone in 2015 versus a cell phone in 2025.
Now, of course, cell phones in 2025 are better than they were in 2015, but they're not really that much better.
cues.zh: 2025 當然更好，但沒好那麼多。

cues.en: So the improvements have all been marginal in the ten years between 2015 and 2025.
cues.zh: 所以 2015 到 2025，改善都只是邊際的。

cues.en: They're a bit faster.
cues.zh: 快一點，

cues.en: The cameras are a bit better.
cues.zh: 相機好一點，

cues.en: They have a bit better memory.
cues.zh: 記憶體好一點。

cues.en: My point is that the tech development was so impressively incredible in the ten years between 2005 and
cues.zh: 重點是，2005 到

cues.en: 2015, but the development between the same amount of time, the same ten year window from 2015 to 2025
cues.zh: 2015 的十年發展驚人，但同樣十年的 2015 到 2025，

cues.en: has just not been that impressive.
cues.zh: 沒有那麼令人驚豔。

cues.en: So now the question is thinking about the change in AI and in particular language models from 2015 to
cues.zh: 接著，想 AI，尤其語言模型，2015 到

cues.en: Those ten years, that ten year span has been unbelievable and explosive, and the difference in capabilities is just mind boggling.
cues.zh: 那十年難以置信、爆炸性成長，能力差異驚人。

cues.en: It's like science fiction.
cues.zh: 像科幻。

cues.en: But here's the question what is going to be the difference in capabilities between 2025 and 2035?
cues.zh: 但問題是，2025 到 2035，能力會差多少？

cues.en: Is that going to be just as big of a change, or are we only going to see marginal improvements?
cues.zh: 一樣巨大，還是只有邊際改善？

cues.en: Again, I do not know the answer to this question and no one else does.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，我不知道，也沒人知道。

cues.en: But I do know that trying to predict tech development ten years out, based on extrapolating from the previous ten years just doesn't make any sense to me.
cues.zh: 但僅靠前十年外推後十年科技，我覺得沒道理。

cues.en: So why all the hype?
cues.zh: 為什麼這麼多炒作？

cues.en: Who is doing all the hyping and who should we believe?
cues.zh: 誰在炒，該信誰？

cues.en: The thing is that many people with different opinions and different attitudes about AI development all have different motivations to hype the future potential of AI.
cues.zh: 不同觀點、態度的人，都有不同動機，誇大 AI 未來潛能。

cues.en: In this slide, I will distinguish between groups called the boomers and the boomers.
cues.zh: 這張分成 boomers 與 doomers，樂觀派與末日派。

cues.en: Boomers here is not referring to the generation of older people, which is what you probably normally associate with the term boomer.
cues.zh: 這裡 boomer 不是通常想到的嬰兒潮世代。

cues.en: An AI boomer is someone who believes that we're only just getting started with AI intelligence capabilities,
cues.zh: AI boomer 相信，我們的智慧能力才剛開始，

cues.en: and the future will be amazing and explosive in ways that we cannot possibly imagine now.
cues.zh: 未來驚人、爆炸，現在無法想像。

cues.en: And AI systems will be much more powerful than any group of humans.
cues.zh: AI 會比任何人類群體強大。

cues.en: A lot of these boomers are hyping up their own AI development because they own or work for AI development companies, so of course they need media attention.
cues.zh: 很多樂觀派擁有、或任職 AI 公司，所以炒自家發展，當然需要媒體關注、

cues.en: Venture capital investments increasing number of users, and so on.
cues.zh: 創投、更多使用者等等。

cues.en: Imagine if you started up an AI company and you went to a bunch of potential investors and told them
cues.zh: 假設創業，向潛在投資人說，

cues.en: that you think that we've already almost reached peak AI capabilities and that your models will be really solid, good quality, but only marginally better than what we already have available.
cues.zh: 能力差不多到頂了，你的模型紮實、品質好，但只比現有稍好。

cues.en: Now, that might be honestly what you believe.
cues.zh: 也許你真的相信，

cues.en: That might be what the future turns out to be, but you're not going to get any funding if you're selling that story.
cues.zh: 未來也真的如此，但這種故事拿不到投資。

cues.en: Other people hype AI because they're using it to generate clicks online for advertisement revenue, more followers on social media or some other personal motivations.
cues.zh: 也有人靠炒作取得點擊、廣告收入、社群追蹤，或其他個人動機。

cues.en: So those are the AI boomers.
cues.zh: 這是 AI 樂觀派。

cues.en: Then we have AI Doomers, and these are people who are gravely concerned about AI risks to prosperity, safety, privacy, and possibly life itself.
cues.zh: 再來末日派，非常擔憂繁榮、安全、隱私，甚至生命風險。

cues.en: So they are also hyping the development of AI capabilities because they want to convince people and
cues.zh: 他們也誇大能力發展，想說服民眾、

cues.en: governments and other regulatory agencies and funding bodies and so on, to support immediate action
cues.zh: 政府、監管與資助機構，支持立即

cues.en: on creating laws and regulations to ensure that AI remains safe and beneficial to humanity and controlled by humans.
cues.zh: 立法規範，確保 AI 安全、有益、受人類控制，

cues.en: And for example, instead of letting our economic and military decisions be made by future AI.
cues.zh: 而非讓未來 AI 決定經濟、軍事。

cues.en: But here's the thing we live in the present.
cues.zh: 但我們活在現在。

cues.en: We can gather data from the past.
cues.zh: 能收集過去資料，

cues.en: We can try to extrapolate about what might happen in the future, but we cannot know what's going to happen in the future.
cues.zh: 試著外推未來，卻不能知道未來。

cues.en: That goes for world events, that goes for our lives, and it goes for the capabilities of AI.
cues.zh: 世界事件、人生、AI 能力，都一樣。

cues.en: Okay, maybe it's a little bit extreme to say that we cannot know what's going to happen in the future.
cues.zh: 好，也許說不能知道未來，有點極端。

cues.en: I am 100% sure that I, in five years from now, will be better than I right now.
cues.zh: 我百分之百確定，五年後 AI 會比現在好。

cues.en: But what I don't know is whether the I in five years will be unbelievably smarter than humans in every
cues.zh: 不知道的是，會不會在每個領域都難以想像地勝過人類，

cues.en: domain, or whether I, in five years from now, will just be slightly better, slightly faster, and slightly cheaper than what we have now.
cues.zh: 還是只稍好、稍快、稍便宜。

cues.en: Let's think about some other predictions about the future that people have made in the past.
cues.zh: 想想過去其他未來預測。

cues.en: We don't have flying cars.
cues.zh: 我們沒有飛天車。

cues.en: The average human lifespan has increased and that's great, but we don't really live past 90 or 100 years old.
cues.zh: 平均壽命提高，很好，但沒有真正活超過九十、一百歲。

cues.en: We do not have colonies on the moon or on Mars or under the sea.
cues.zh: 沒有月球、火星、海底殖民地。

cues.en: We don't all use Bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies.
cues.zh: 也不是大家都用比特幣、加密貨幣。

cues.en: We don't have all of our nutritional needs provided once a day in a pill.
cues.zh: 沒有每天一顆藥丸，就滿足全部營養。

cues.en: And somehow, some way, humanity survived Y2K.
cues.zh: 而且人類不知怎地，活過了 Y2K。

cues.en: Okay, I hope I didn't come across as sounding too negative or too critical in this video.
cues.zh: 希望這支沒有太負面、太苛刻。

cues.en: I think it is very possible that the future of AI will be incredible and incredibly terrifying.
cues.zh: 我認為，AI 未來很可能驚人，也極度可怕。

cues.en: But I think it is wrong to make the assumption that it must be as much better in the future as the present is from the past.
cues.zh: 但不能假定，未來一定會像過去到現在一樣大幅改善。

cues.en: Any time you hear about people talking about the future of AI capabilities, you really need to think
cues.zh: 聽別人預測時，必須批判思考，

cues.en: critically about why they might be making that prediction, what their predictions are based on, and
cues.zh: 為何這樣預測、依據是什麼，

cues.en: what they stand to gain from making these very bold claims about things that haven't happened, and
cues.zh: 對尚未發生的事大膽宣稱，有什麼利益，

cues.en: long term extrapolations based on highly complex, highly dynamical, highly non-linear and highly mysterious systems.
cues.zh: 以及對複雜、動態、非線性、神祕系統做長期外推的問題。

cues.en: By the way, if you have any thoughts or reactions or disagreements with what I've said, feel free to post them in the Q&A.
cues.zh: 有想法、反應、不同意，歡迎貼問答區。

cues.en: I and your fellow students are curious to know what you think.
cues.zh: 我和同學都好奇你的看法。
